claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 16 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 16 and in the 20-week extension period
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex
expected_eligibility.reason: Claimant lives in the UK; Child is 16 and in the 20-week extension period; Child lives with claimant; Child is not in local authority care; Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation; Child is not fostered; Child does not work 24+ hours/week; Child has not started an apprenticeship in England; Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right
circumstances: Child is 16 and in the 20-week extension period
Child is not in local authority care

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're claiming for?**

- Are they **under 16 years old**?
- Are they **16 to 19 years old**?
- Are they **20 years old or older**?

Please let me know the age category of each child you'd like me to assess.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi there! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who just turned 16 recently. So yes, they're in that 16 to 19 age range.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have **Alex, who is 16 years old** - that's great information to start with.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age range, I need to check whether they're in full-time education or training, as this affects eligibility. Let me navigate to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **Alex's current education or training status**:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In full-time education or approved training** (e.g., school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** (not in education/training and didn't recently leave)?

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex actually left school recently. They finished their course and are currently registered with the local careers service to figure out what they want to do next - whether that's college, an apprenticeship, or something else.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail! So Alex has recently left school and is registered with the careers service while deciding their next steps. That means they fall into the "left education recently" category.

Let me check the extension eligibility rules for this situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! This is important. There's a **20-week extension** available for young people who have recently left education and registered with a qualifying service.

Based on what you've told me, Alex:
- ✓ Has left approved education/training (finished their school course)
- ✓ Is registered with a qualifying service (the local careers service)

**I need to confirm the timing:** 

**How long ago did Alex leave school?** Is it **within the last 20 weeks**? 

Also, just to confirm - **is Alex still 16 years old** (the extension applies until age 18 or the end of the 20-week period, whichever comes first)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, Alex is still 16 - they only just turned 16 recently actually. 

And they left school just a few weeks ago, so yes, definitely within the last 20 weeks. They registered with the careers service pretty much straight away after finishing up.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's really helpful. So Alex:
- ✓ Is 16 years old
- ✓ Left school just a few weeks ago (within the 20-week window)
- ✓ Registered with the careers service straight away

This means Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension. Now let me check the next eligibility requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **Alex's work situation**:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

For example, Alex could be doing part-time work, casual work, or no paid work - as long as it's under 24 hours per week, that's fine.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all at the moment. They're just focusing on figuring out their next steps with the careers service right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So Alex isn't working at all, which means they're definitely working less than 24 hours per week. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **whether Alex is receiving certain benefits in their own right**:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of the following benefits directly:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

If Alex isn't claiming any of these benefits themselves, that's what we're looking for. What's Alex's situation here?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in their own name. They're still living at home with me and not claiming anything themselves.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex isn't receiving ESA or Universal Credit in their own name. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check **Alex's apprenticeship status**. This has regional variations, so it's important to get this right.

**Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship?**

If yes, I'll need to know:
- Which country/region is the apprenticeship in? (England, Scotland, or Wales)
- What type of apprenticeship is it?

If no, then we can move on to the next stage!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. Like I said, they just left school and are working with the careers service to figure out what they want to do next - whether that'll be college, an apprenticeship, or something else. But they haven't started anything yet.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So Alex is not currently in an apprenticeship - they're still exploring their options. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **your residency status**, as you're the claimant. There are several possible paths that can qualify you:

**Which of the following best describes your situation:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward option
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (with various sub-categories depending on your circumstances - working, job-seeking, studying, sufficient resources, or family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here in England with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward. You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **your responsibility for Alex**. Responsibility can be shown in a few ways:

**Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** - You share a home together
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for their food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc., at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount
3. **You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement** - If there's a formal arrangement for supporting Alex

Based on what you've already told me (you live at home in England with Alex), it sounds like you live together. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you live with Alex, which means you're clearly responsible for them. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **whether anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex**:

**Is there another person (such as Alex's other parent, or someone else) who is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or who might also be claiming?**

- No other claimant?
- Another person is claiming, but you both agree that you should be the claimant?
- Another person is claiming, and there's a dispute about who should claim?

What's the situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - no one else is claiming or planning to claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So you're the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me continue to the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **Alex's living situation**:

**Which of the following best describes where Alex is living:**

1. **In hospital** - Receiving inpatient care
2. **In care** - In a children's home or similar care facility
3. **Fostered** - With foster carers
4. **Living normally** - At home with you or in normal accommodation

What's the situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally - they're at home with me, just like I mentioned earlier.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me continue to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is the final check! I need to confirm:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, you're paying for Alex's housing and upkeep yourself, and the council isn't providing financial support for this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm covering everything myself since Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final piece of information I needed. Based on everything you've told me, I can now provide you with your eligibility decision.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me report your final eligibility decision:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

Congratulations! You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Why Alex Qualifies:**
- ✓ Alex is 16 years old (recently turned 16)
- ✓ Recently left full-time education (just a few weeks ago)
- ✓ Registered with the local careers service within the 20-week extension period
- ✓ Not working full-time (not working at all)
- ✓ Not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
- ✓ Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✓ Living at home with you

**Why You Qualify as the Claimant:**
- ✓ You normally live in the UK
- ✓ You are responsible for Alex (living together)
- ✓ You are the sole claimant
- ✓ The council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year (this doesn't affect eligibility, but may mean tax adjustments)
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

For more information and to apply, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) Alex is 16 years old and has recently left full-time education within the last 20 weeks; (2) Alex registered with the local careers service immediately after leaving school, which qualifies for the 20-week extension; (3) Alex is not working or is working less than 24 hours per week; (4) Alex is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in their own right; (5) Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (6) You (the claimant) normally live in the UK and are responsible for Alex by living with them; (7) You are the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Alex is living at home with you in normal accommodation; and (9) The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Alex meets the qualifying criteria as a 16-year-old who has recently left full-time education and is registered with the careers service within the 20-week extension period. You meet all the claimant requirements: you normally live in the UK, you are responsible for Alex (living together), you are the sole claimant, and the council is not funding Alex's accommodation. There are no disqualifying factors, and all eligibility requirements have been satisfied."
